sources.title: Java Virtual Machine Technology Overview, Java SE 24
Python 3.14 py_compile — Compile Python source files
Python 3.14 dis — Disassembler for Python bytecode

claims.text: A typical Clang/GCC-style C++ AOT toolchain uses preprocess/compile/assemble/link stages and emits target-specific object/native code; portability generally means rebuilding source for the intended target rather than treating one native binary as universally portable.
javac compiles Java source declarations into class files that run on the JVM.

The JVM class-file format is hardware/OS independent, while a JVM implementation may interpret or translate JVM code at load time or during execution into host native instructions; these are implementation strategies rather than mutually exclusive language labels.

HotSpot can launch through an interpreter, profile running code, compile hot portions adaptively, and deoptimize optimized code when assumptions no longer hold; this supports the candidate's bounded warm-up/JIT resource-cost discussion rather than an unconditional JVM requirement.
CPython compiles source/code objects to CPython bytecode and can cache source compilation as .pyc byte-code files; import may reuse cached bytecode after validating it.
CPython bytecode is an implementation detail and is not guaranteed to remain compatible across Python VMs or Python releases.

CPython runtime memory management includes reference counting supplemented by cyclic garbage collection, supporting the candidate's scoped statement that runtime object/memory semantics can contribute to execution cost.

The cited C++ target model, JVM implementation flexibility/adaptive compilation, and CPython implementation-specific bytecode together support comparing performance and portability conditionally by toolchain, runtime, native-library boundaries and workload instead of asserting a universal speed ranking.

findings: The fixed candidate bytes were reviewed source-first against the current canonical/source rows and primary official documentation before writer rationale or historical review/remediation records were consulted.
The candidate answers the shared source question directly by comparing translation targets, runtime execution and portability rather than assigning simplistic compiled/interpreted labels.
C++ behavior is scoped to a typical AOT toolchain; Java behavior separates javac from JVM runtime strategy; Python behavior is explicitly scoped to CPython and .pyc/bytecode implementation details.
Version- and implementation-sensitive claims are bounded to Clang-style toolchains, JVM/HotSpot where appropriate, and CPython; performance claims remain workload-dependent.
